newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 14-SUNDAY, APRIL 20.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 14-SUNDAY, APRIL 20.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
LUXEMBOURG - EU fisheries ministers meet (Monday-Tuesday).

BRUSSELS - Inter-governmental conference representatives meet (Monday-Tuesday). MOSCOW - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov to discuss next round of talks for NATO/Russia charter (Tuesday).

VALETTA, Malta - Foreign ministers from the EU and 12 Mediterranean countries meet for the Euro-Med Conference, the follow-up to 1994's Barcelona Accord (Tuesday-Wednesday). Middle East crisis likely to feature prominently. Closing news conference on Wednesday.
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - EP and Council Conciliation Committee meets on "TV without frontiers directive" (Wednesday).
LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers meet (Thursday); discussions cover a code of conduct for companies that close plants, burden of proof in sex discrimination suits and job quotas for women.
AMSTERDAM - EU environment ministers hold informal meeting (Thursday-Sunday); discussions cover relationship between the environment, the economy and small and medium-sized enterprises.
MONDAY, APRIL 14
LUXEMBOURG - Fisheries Council (1000/0800 GMT) (and Tuesday).
Agenda includes:

- Proposal for a Council decision on objectives and detailed rules for restructuring the Community fisheries sector for the period from 1 January 1997 to 31 December 1999 with a view to achieving a balance on a sustainable basis between resources and their exploitation (MAGPs IV).
- Proposal for a Council regulation on autonomous Community tariff quotas for certain fishery products.

- Proposal for a Council regulation on amendment of regulation (CE) No 3901/97 fixing, for certain stocks and groups of fish stocks, the total allowable catches for 1997 and certain conditions under which they may be fished (allocation of Atlanto-Scandian herring and horse mackerel).
- Proposal for a Council decision on specific measure to encourage Italian fishermen to diversify out of certain fishing activities.
- Other business:
- Report from the Commission on the application of the Community system for fisheries and aquaculture;
- Oral presentation by the Commission on fisheries agreements - Current situation and perspectives;
- Reflection paper by the Spanish delegation on drift-nets.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental conference representatives meet (and Tuesday).
LONDON (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner de Silguy attends and addresses European Bank for Reconstruction and Development annual assembly.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1300 GMT) Foreign Affairs - Commissioner Brittan gives address on common foreign and security policy (1630/1430 GMT);
Budget;
Research/Energy;
Transport;
Culture/Youth;

Development - Court of Auditors member Jan Karlsson presents report on EU's humanitarian aid at 1515/1315 GMT; World Bank representative to the European institutions Spiros Voyadzis attends at 1700/1500 GMT;
Rules of Procedure;
Petitions;
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Monetary Subcommittee and Legal Affairs and Environment Committees hold public hearing on "The introduction of the euro and consumer protection" (1500/1300 GMT).

LUXEMBOURG - Finnish Justice Minister Kari Haekaemies meets Court of Justice President Gil Carlos Rodriguez Iglesias at 1130/0930 GMT; discussions focus on the organisation and role of the Court of Justice in the context of the inter-governmental conference and the need for cooperation between the Court and the national legal systems of the member states - followed by a news conference at 1600/1400 GMT. Contact: Tom Kennedy (352) 4303 3355.

LEIDEN, Netherlands - The Philip Morris Institute (PMI) holds conference on "How much popular support is there for the EU?". Contact: PMI (322) 732 1156. Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 2/4 - Tuesday)
TUESDAY, APRIL 15
LUXEMBOURG - Fisheries Council continues.
MOSCOW - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana meets Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov to discuss next round of talks for NATO-Russia charter.

VALETTA, Malta (EXPANDED ITEM) - Meeting of foreign ministers from the EU and 12 Mediterranean countries for the Euro-Med Conference, the follow-up to 1994's Barcelona Accord, begins at 1500/1300 GMT (first of two days). Middle East crisis likely to feature prominently. European Commissioner Marin attends.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus meets WEU Secretary Jose Cutileiro at 0855/0655 GMT, followed by news conference at 0945/0745; meets EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles at 1100/0900 GMT, followed by joint news conference at 1140/0940 GMT; meets Commission President Santer at 1215/1015 GMT.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Foreign Affairs - Head of fact-finding mission to Belarus gives address on the situation in Belarus at 1030/0830 GMT;
Budget;
Research/Energy;
Transport - meeting with central and eastern European countries national parliament representatives - exchange of views on the Helsinki declaration;
Culture/Youth;
Development - ECHO Director Navarro gives address on the outcome of the world food summit at 0930/0730 GMT;
Monetary Subcommittee;
Rules of Procedure;
Petitions;
- (1500/1300 GMT) Agriculture - Commissioner Fischler gives address on recommendations of the committee of inquiry into BSE at 1730/1530 GMT;
Research/Energy;
Legal Affairs;
Employment/Social Affairs;
Transport - Commissioner Kinnock gives address on road safety; trans-European network corridors; Commissioner Papoutsis gives address on tourism programme 1994-1998 (PHILOXIA) at 1700/1500 GMT;
Environment;
Culture/Youth - Commissioner Oreja gives address on the EU's information policy;
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Rules of Procedure Committee holds public hearing on "Financing and operations of the intergroups" (0900/0700 GMT).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Research and Energy Committee holds public hearing on "Research for Europe: from the 4th to the 5th R&TD" Framework Programme (0915/0715 GMT).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Agriculture Committee holds public hearing on "What future for the olive tree after 3000 years of history?" (1500/1300 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Budgetary Control and Civil Liberties Committees hold public hearing on "Protection of the European taxpayer - Towards a common legal and judicial area" (1500/1300 GMT) (and Wednesday). Speakers include: European Commission President Santer, EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles, European Commissioner Gradin. Topics include: the EU's response to the attack on its finances by organised crime; from safeguarding the Community budget to protecting the public.

BRUSSELS - Inuit Circumpolar Conference holds conference on "Wildlife management, indigenous peoples and the world of politics" (1000/0800 GMT). Topics discussed are the objectives of import bans and international trading obligations: the case of EU import prohibitions; indigenous peoples' concerns with animal welfare and trade restrictions; the objectives of animal welfare groups and the realities of wildlife management; sustainability and the realities of life. Venue: EP, Belliard room 53. Contact: Inuit Circumpolar Conference, Greenland (299) 2 36 32.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds workshop on "Identifying the priorities for energy conservation" (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes: myths and realities in energy conservation: what is really needed; energy conservation in business: potentials and obstacles; the impacts of liberalisation on energy efficiency and renewables; integration of climate change objectives; how the necessary long-term consensus on climate change policy can be established. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - The European Energy Foundation holds dinner debate on "Medium and long term security of supply of oil and gas in Europe" (1900/1700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Europa. Contact: The European Energy Foundation (322) 773 9522.

ATHENS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) President Tom Jenkins meets Greek President Costas Simitis; discussions focus on socio-professional contribution to the European decision-making process and on ECOSOC in the institutional architecture at the dawn of the inter-governmental conference - followed by a joint news conference at 1345/1145 GMT. for Tuesday, April 15-Thursday, April 24
(All venues Luxembourg, Plateau de Kirchberg)
TUESDAY, APRIL 15

COURT OF JUSTICE, PLENARY COURT ((0930/0730 GMT) - Oral procedure C-141/96 Langhorst: taxation. Request for preliminary ruling. Interpretation of article 22, paragraph 3(c) and subsidiarily article 21, paragraph 1(c) of sixth Council VAT directive 77/388/EEC of May 17, 1977, on the harmonisation of member states' legislation on turnover tax. Common VAT system: uniform basis of assessment. Document serving as invoice. Credit notice issued by buyer and not contested by seller as regards the rate and amount of VAT indicated therein. - (1000/0800 GMT) Oral procedure C-85/96 Martinez Sala: free movement of persons. Request for preliminary ruling. Interpretation of article 7, paragraph 2 of Council regulation 1612/68, of October 15, 1968, on freedom of movement for workers within the Community as well as of articles 2 and 4, paragraph 1(h) of Council regulation 1408/71 of June 14, 1971, on social security schemes for employed persons and their families moving within the EU as amended and updated by Council regulation 2001/83 of June 2, 1983. Notion of "salaried worker". Person without employment, dependent on social assistance for several years. Notion of family benefit. School benefit paid to a parent without a professional activity towards the maintenance of a small child.

FOURTH CHAMBER ((0930/0730 GMT) - Judgment C-105/95 Daut: free movement of goods. Request for preliminary ruling. Interpretation of EC treaty articles 30 and 36. Interpretation of Council directive 64/433/EEC of June 26, 1964 on health problems affecting intra-Community trade in fresh meat as amended by directive 91/497/EEC - Interpretation of 77/99/EEC of December 21, 1976 on health problems affecting intra-Community trade of meat-based products as modified and codified by Council directive 92/5/EEC - restriction on intra-Community trade of meat mechanically separated not having undergone heat treatment. Sanitary production and marketing conditions. - Judgment C-272/95 Deutsches Milch-Kontor: agriculture. Request for preliminary ruling. Interpretation of EC treaty articles 9, 12, 16 and 95 as well as of article 2 of Council regulation 1624/76 of July 2, 1976, on special arrangements for the payment of aid for skimmed-milk powder denatured or processed into compound feeding stuffs in the territory of another member state as amended by regulation 1726/79 of July 26, 1976. Inspection measures for the quality and composition of the product. Frequency of inspections through sampling. Inspection costs payable by exporter.

FIFTH CHAMBER (0930/0730 GMT) - Judgment C-151/96 Commission v/ Ireland: free movement of persons. Non-respect. Breach of articles 6, 48, 52 and 58 of the EC treaty and of article 7 of Commission regulation 1251/70 of June 29, 1970, on the right of workers to reside on the territory of a member state after having occupied a job and of article 7 of Council directive 75/34/EEC of December 17, 1974, on the right of member state citizens to reside on the territory of another member state after exercising an unsalaried activity. Registration of vessels other than fishing vessels. Right to fly the Irish flag.

SIXTH CHAMBER (0930/0730 GMT) - Judgment C-22/94 Irish Farmers Association: agriculture. Request for preliminary ruling. Validity of article 1, paragraph 3(g) of Council regulation 816/92 of March 31, 1992, amending regulation 804/68 on the common organisation of the market in milk and milk products and of article 3 of Council regulation 3950/92 of December 28, 1992, establishing an additional levy in the milk and milk products sector. Exclusion of reference quantities attributed for 1992/1993, the granting of which was temporarily suspended. Absence of compensation for producers. - Judgment C-27/97 Bakers of Nailsea: agriculture. Request for preliminary ruling. Validity of Council directive 64/433/EEC of June 26, 1964, on health problems affecting intra-Community trade in fresh meat and of Council directive 85/73/EEC of January 29, 1985, on the financing of health inspections and controls on fresh meats and poultry. Health inspections ante mortem. Level of fees. - Judgment C-292/95 Spain v/ Commission: state aid. Annulment of Commission decision of July 6, 1995, prolonging with retroactive effect from January 1, 1995, the decision of December 23, 1992, on the Community framework of state aid to the automobile sector. - Opinion C-138/96 Commission v/ Germany: agriculture. Non-respect. Failure to have transposed within the prescribed period Council directive 92/116/EEC of December 17, 1992, amending and updating Council directive 71/118/EEC on health problems in the trade of fresh meat and poultry. - Opinion C-150/95 Portugal v/ Commission: agriculture. Partial annulment of Commission regulation 307/95 of February 14, 1995, establishing final corrected regional reference amounts for producers of soya beans, rape seed, colza seed and sunflower seed for the 1994/1995 marketing year in that it reduces by 20 percent the final regional reference amounts for sunflower seeds in Portugal. Violation of the membership act, the Blair House agreement and Council regulation 1765/92 of June 30, 1992, establishing a support scheme for producers of certain arable crops, removing from small Portuguese producers the obligation of fallowing land. Discrimination on grounds of nationality. Exclusion of Portuguese producers from the benefits of compensation for overproduction and non-use in the Community as a whole.

COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE, FIFTH CHAMBER (0930/0730 GMT) - Judgment T-390/94 Schroeder and others v/ Commission: agriculture. Action for damages. Non-contractual responsibility of the Community resulting from Commission adaptation of several decisions on protection measures against classic swine fever in Germany.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 16

COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE, FIFTH CHAMBER (0915/0715 GMT) - Judgment T-20/90 Hartmann v/ Council and Commission: agriculture. Action for damages. Council regulation 2187/93 of July 22,1 1993, providing for the offer of compensation to certain milk or milk product producers temporarily prevented from exercising their activity. - Judgment T-541/93 Connaughton v/ Council: agriculture. Annulment of article 8 and 14 of Council regulation 2187/93 of July 22, 1993, providing for the offer of compensation to certain milk or milk product producers temporarily prevented from exercising their activity. - Judgment T-554/93 Saint and others v/ Council and Commission: agriculture. Annulment of article 8 paragraph 2(a) and 14 of Council regulation 2187/93 of July 22, 1993, providing for the offer of compensation to certain milk or milk product producers temporarily prevented from exercising their activity. Limitation of compensation through regulatory means. Limitation of action. Partial abandonment of action by 586 claimants.
THURSDAY, APRIL 17

COURT OF JUSTICE, PLENARY COURT (0930/0730 GMT) - Opinion C-296/95 EMU Tabac: taxation. Request for preliminary ruling. Interpretation of article 8 of Council directive 92/12/EEC of February 25, 1992, on arrangements for the detention, circulation and control of products subject to excise duty. Tobacco products acquired for the specific needs of an individual in member state A, by his agent in member state B who provides the transport towards member state A. Exclusion of collection of excise duty by member state A.

FIRST CHAMBER (0930/0730 GMT) - Judgment C-138/95 P Campo Ebro Industrial v/ Council: agriculture. Appeal against Court judgment (first chamber) rendered February 21, 1995, in case T-472/93, opposing Campo Ebro Industrial and others to the Council. Annulment of Council regulation 3814/92 of December 28, 1992, modifying regulation 1785/81 and applied in Spain to prices in the sugar sector provided for by this regulation. Damages caused to isoglucose producers resulting from the absence of compensation for the aligning of sugar prices on common prices. Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 3/4 - Wednesday-Thursday)
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 16
VALETTA, Malta (NEW ITEM) - Meeting of foreign ministers from the EU and 12 Mediterranean countries continues (second of two days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) EU/Mediterranean political relations.
- (1000/0900 GMT) EU/Mediterranean economic relations.
- (1100/0900 GMT) EU/Mediterranean social and cultural relations.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Closing ceremony and news conference.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0700 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Bangemann communication on European initiative on electronic commerce.
- Commissioner Bangemann communication on competitiveness of communication and information technologies industries.
- Commissioner Bangemann communication on standardisation of competitive performance - implementation of an instrument at the operators' disposal.
- Commissioner Kinnock proposal for directive on airport fees.
- Commissioner Brittan communication on market access for less developed countries.
- Commissioner Flynn green paper on the partnership for a new work organisation.
- Commissioner Monti proposal for EP and Council directive modifying Council directive 93/6/EEC on capital adequacy of investment companies and credit establishments.
- Commissioners Gradin, Flynn, Wulf-Mathies, Fischler, Bonino and Liikanen joint communication on SEM 2000: eligibility of expenses in structural funds.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - EP and Council Conciliation Committee meets on "TV without frontiers directive". European Commissioner Oreja attends.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles meets Spanish Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio (1730/1530 GMT).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Agriculture;
Research/Energy;
Legal Affairs - Dutch Justice Minister Winifred Sorgdrager at 1100/0900 GMT;
Employment/Social Affairs;
Transport;
Environment;
Youth/Culture;
Development;
- (1500/1300 GMT) External Economic Relations;
Economic;
Employment/Social Affairs - Commissioner Flynn gives progress report on April 17 Social Affairs and Employment Council;
Fisheries;
Women's Rights;

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Institutional Affairs Committee holds joint meeting with national parliament members (1500/1300 GMT) (and Thursday). Topics include the democratic deficit in practice: the problems of democratic control facing the EP and national parliaments; improved monitoring techniques in the different parliaments; improved cooperation between the national parliaments and the Union.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Employment and Social Affairs Committee holds public hearing on "Frontier workers - Problems and solutions" (1500/1300 GMT).

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Norway - Outside of the EU" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is Ambassador of Norway to the EU Einar Bull. Venue: CPES. Contact: CEPS (322) 3911.

BRUSSELS - Schleswig-Holstein Economics, Technology and Transport Minister Peer Steinbrueck addresses the fourth maritime dialogue conference on "Short sea shipping in the Baltic Sea - Importance and development of transport chains" (1800/1600 GMT). Venue: House of the new German Laender, 80 Blvd Saint Michel. Contact: House of the new German Laender (322) 285 4657.
BRUSSELS - Aeronautica holds "European air transport conference" (and Thursday). Venue: Sheraton Towers. Contact: Aeronautica (44) 181 893 3795.

MAASTRICHT (EXPANDED ITEM) - The National Committee for International Cooperation and Sustainable Development and the Dutch foreign affairs ministry host conference on "Public support for international cooperation" (and Thursday). This meeting will bring together representatives of national governments of the member states, the European Commission and NGOs for an exchange of ideas and experiences on obtaining public support for development cooperation. European Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro attends.
THURSDAY, APRIL 17
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - Social Affairs Council (1000/0800 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Employment and Labour Market Committee work programme.
- Proposal for a directive: "Burden of proof in cases of discrimination based on sex".

- Proposal for a directive amending directive 76/207/EEC on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women as regards access to employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions (Kalanke Ruling).
- Workers information and consultation:
- Commission information on "Davignon" working group;
- Presidency information on the outcome of the informal Social Affairs Council held in Rotterdam March 14-15 and especially the round table with social partners at a European level on April 15.
- Commission information on "Modernising and improve social protection in the EU".
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Economic;
External Economic Relations - Commissioner van den Broek gives address on Turkey, former Yugoslavia and reform of PHARE programme;
Legal Affairs;
Fisheries - Commissioner Bonino and EUROPECHE/COGECA representatives discuss the common fisheries policy after 2002;
Womens' Rights;
- (1500/1300 GMT) External Economic Relations - European Free Trade Area Secretary General Kjartan Johannsson gives addres at 1600/1500 GMT;
Fisheries.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Union of Industrial and Employers Confederations of Europe (UNICE) holds press lunch to present UNICE's views and priorities for the inter-governmental conference as it approaches the final stages (1245/1045 GMT). Venue: UNICE, 40 rue Josef II. Contact: UNICE (322) 237 6511.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Belgian Senate Foreign Affairs Committee Vice President Anne-Marie Lizin and Action in the Mediterranean President Simone Susskind host conference on "Give peace a chance - Women speak out in Cyprus" (1100/0900 GMT) (to Saturday). Venue: Palais d'Egmont. Contact: Catherine Portevin (322) 346 2797.

BRUSSELS - Katholieke Universiteit Brussel (KU) holds international relations lecture on "Mixed signals: Central bank independence, wage bargaining". Speaker is Harvard University Government Professor Peter Hall. Venue: KU Brussels. Contact: KU (322) 412 4211. Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 4/4 - Friday-Sunday)
FRIDAY, APRIL 18
AMSTERDAM (EXPANDED ITEM) - Informal Environment Council (to Sunday). Discussions cover relationship between the environment, the economy and small and medium-sized enterprises.
BRUSSELS - European Committee for Banking Standards (ECBS) holds news conference at 1200/1000 GMT. Venue: ECBS offices, 12 avenue de Tervuren. Contact: ECBS (322)733 3533.

BOLOGNA, Italy - European Commission and Committee of the Regions hold joint seminar on "Climate change, energy and strategic response at local and regional level" (0830/0630 GMT). Venue: Piazza Maggiore 6. Contact: Comunicatori Associati (39) 51 276211.

MAASTRICHT (EXPANDED ITEM) - Dutch Development Cooperation Minister Jan Pronk hosts a meeting of development ministers from the EU and African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries to discuss the future of the Lome convention, which lays down the political, trade and aid relations between the two sides (and Saturday). European Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro attends.

VIENNA (NEW ITEM) - Union of European Federalists (UEF) holds conference on "The EU: The challenge of the 21st century - for a European constituent assembly" (first of three days). Venue: University. Contact: UEF (322) 512 1012.
Agenda includes:
- (1430/1230 GMT) UEF President Francesco Rossolillo give opening address.
- (1445/1245 GMT) Austrian Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel gives address.
- (1500/1300 GMT) MEP Elmar Brok and Austrian Social Affairs Minister Eleonore Hostasch give address on "The future development of the EU".
SATURDAY, APRIL 19

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Closing news conference of the conference on "Give peace a chance - Women speak out in Cyprus" (1130/0930 GMT). Venue: Palais d'Egmont. Contact: Catherine Portevin (322) 346 2797.

VIENNA (NEW ITEM) - Union of European Federalists (UEF) holds conference on "The EU: The challenge of the 21st century - for a European constituent assembly" (second of three days). Venue: University. Contact: UEF (322) 512 1012.
Agenda includes:
- (0930/0730 GMT) Working groups on:
- Inter-governmental conference and European constituent assembly.
- EMU and employment.
- Enlargement and common foreign and security policy.
SUNDAY, APRIL 20
No events scheduled.
